findings.title: Editors can publish policy documents, which resets the owner's approval and closes checkout
findings.evidence: content_assert_publisher (never redefined) admits `s.role in ('owner', 'editor')` for every collection; content_versions_insert (line 38) is the same; `policies` was added to the enum later (20260927160000:32) with no owner restriction, and policies_reset_approval (20260930120000_audit_fixes.sql:141-145) clears finance.commerce_settings.policy_revisions on any new seq of an approved policy.
findings.impact: An editor account (or a stolen editor session at aal1, no TOTP) publishes a new seq of the store, delivery or refund policy from the admin or by calling rpc/publish_version directly; the trigger wipes policy_revisions and checkout answers POLICIES_NOT_CONFIGURED to every buyer until the owner re-approves at aal2. The same role can replace the privacy text buyers read with no approval at all (a privacy document outside the approved set does not reset). PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:51 says the owner configures policies; src/admin/collections/policies.ts:5-8 says editors draft and publish them.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide the rule, then enforce it in SQL: make content_assert_publisher take the collection and require an active owner when it is 'policies' (publish_version, schedule_version, and the content_versions_insert policy), and align DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:51 or policies.ts.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 X1.1 added the reset; the editor-can-trigger-it consequence was not recorded

findings.title: Hidden list items inside live documents, and their images, are readable with the anon key
findings.evidence: published_documents_public_read: `using (collection <> 'posts' or data -> 'visible' = 'true'::jsonb)` filters rows only; the rooms' hideable lists (movements, reels, brandWall, gallery: src/admin/collections/rooms.ts:62,71,98,156-158; src/admin/fields.ts:278 adds `hidden: true` to an item) stay inside `data`. media_published_ids() (lines 73-79) collects every uuid-shaped string of the row, hidden items included, so media_public_read exposes their id, derivatives and alt_ar too.
findings.impact: The admin's «مخفي» on a gallery photo, a brand logo or a reel hides it from the built page only; anyone with the publishable key (shipped in the static export) reads the item through the Data API and fetches the derivative from the public bucket. Same class as AUDIT-1 S01.1 (hidden post), one level down. Bounded: only content an editor once meant to publish.
findings.proposed_fix: Serve anon from a security_definer view or function that strips `hidden = true` items from `data` before returning it, and derive media_published_ids() from the stripped data; or state in DESIGN/DATA docs that item hiding is presentational only.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S01.1 / S02.4 covered hidden posts only

findings.title: service_role's default table and function privileges are assumed, not set: the model differs between the local stack and a legacy hosted project
findings.evidence: `alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on tables from anon, authenticated;` (and sequences, functions) never names service_role. 20260925090000_audit_and_staff_directory.sql:77-80 says new tables are granted to no API role by default and 'No delete on either table'; artifacts/acceptance/P03/commands.txt:45-46 recorded that the local pg_default_acl still grants service_role Delete/Truncate/References/Trigger on every new relation, and the Supabase changelog 45329 says a project created before 2026-05-30 with the legacy toggle grants select, insert, update, delete to service_role as well.
findings.impact: On the hosted project the real grants of service_role on contacts, media, content_versions, published_documents, staff and audit_events are whatever the project's default ACL was at creation: DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:23 ('no API role, the owner included, has any grant' on contacts) and the migration comments describe the local stack, not the hosted one. Bounded: service_role lives only inside the Edge Functions (which touch only staff and audit_events directly) and bypasses RLS anyway; DELETE on audit_events is still refused by the trigger and TRUNCATE is unreachable through PostgREST.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the model explicit in one forward migration: `alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on tables from service_role;` (and on sequences and functions), keep the explicit grants staff-admin uses (staff select/insert/update, audit_events insert), and run the integration suites to prove nothing relied on the implicit grants.
findings.proof_recipe: On the hosted project (SQL editor as postgres): `select defaclobjtype, defaclacl from pg_default_acl where defaclrole = 'postgres'::regrole and defaclnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace;` then `select has_table_privilege('service_role','public.contacts','select'), has_table_privilege('service_role','public.audit_events','delete'), has_function_privilege('service_role','public.publish_due()','execute');`. Wrong result: any true, or a defaclacl entry naming service_role.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S01.5 fixed the PUBLIC function default only

findings.title: Publishing has no server-side content or media check: the Zod schema and the dangling-media gate run only in the browser
findings.evidence: publish_version checks the actor and the stale seq, then `perform public.content_go_live(...)`, which copies `v.data` as stored. The header of 20260925120000 (lines 5-7) still says the Worker 'validated the data with the collection's Zod schema' and 20260926090000:117-119 says 'restoring one that points at deleted media fails the publish check in src/lib/publish.ts'; both checks moved to the browser (src/lib/admin-publish.ts) with D32 and nothing in SQL repeats them.
findings.impact: An editor calling rpc/publish_version or rpc/schedule_version directly (or an admin build with a bug) takes a version live that the site build cannot render: a room missing required fields, a post whose `visible` is a string (RLS then hides it), or a document naming a media id that media_delete removed meanwhile (the race the migration comment accepts because of the publish check). src/lib/journal.ts:78 then fails the Pages build until a staff member republishes. Editor-trust boundary, so low.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the two comments at least; better, make content_go_live refuse a version whose data references a uuid-shaped media id that is not in public.media, using the same jsonb_path_query as media_published_ids().

findings.title: media_is_published(uuid) is still executable by anon although nothing public calls it
findings.evidence: `grant execute on function public.media_is_published(uuid) to anon;` survives every later `create or replace` (20260927180000:10, 20260930120000:96). The policy now uses media_published_ids() (audit_fixes.sql:92); a grep over src/ and supabase/functions/ finds no caller of media_is_published outside migrations and tests/integration/audit-fixes.test.ts:125, which pins it as expected anon surface.
findings.impact: A public, unthrottled RPC that scans every published document with jsonb_path_exists plus the products table per call: an oracle for 'is this uuid referenced anywhere public' and the per-call amplification AUDIT-1 S02.4 removed from the policy, kept alive as an endpoint. Small today, grows with the journal.
findings.proposed_fix: `revoke execute on function public.media_is_published(uuid) from anon;` and drop it from the expected list in tests/integration/audit-fixes.test.ts:123-127.

findings.title: outbox_replay: a null p_accept_duplicate_risk bypasses the duplicate-risk confirmation
findings.evidence: `v_ambiguous := o.first_attempt_at <= now() - interval '23 hours'; if v_ambiguous and not p_accept_duplicate_risk then raise ...`. With p_accept_duplicate_risk = null, `true and not null` is null and the IF does not fire; the UPDATE then runs with `idempotency_key = gen_random_uuid()` because v_ambiguous is true, and the audit row records acceptedDuplicateRisk: null. The function is granted to authenticated (owner/operations) and takes a plain boolean with no NOT NULL guard.
findings.impact: An owner or operations member calling rpc/outbox_replay with {"p_id": N, "p_accept_duplicate_risk": null} (a hand-written call, or a client that sends null for an unchecked box) replays an ambiguous exhausted or uncertain row past the 23-hour idempotency window with a fresh key and no confirmation: a buyer can receive a receipt or order link twice, which the DATA-AND-SECURITY rule ('an ambiguous send outside that lifetime needs reconciliation before retry') exists to prevent. Staff-only and self-inflicted, so low.
findings.proposed_fix: `if v_ambiguous and not coalesce(p_accept_duplicate_risk, false) then raise ...` (and coalesce in the audit summary).
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 X1.3 added v_ambiguous; the null case was not covered

findings.title: The journal build reads published posts and taxonomies without paging, so PostgREST max_rows (1000) silently truncates the site once the journal grows
findings.evidence: `fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/published_documents?collection=eq.posts&select=...`)` with only the apikey header: no Range header, no next page, and the body is accepted whenever `response.ok`. supabase/config.toml:18 sets `max_rows = 1000` (the hosted default is the same); PostgREST answers 200 with the first 1000 rows and a Content-Range the loader never reads.
findings.impact: When the journal (or the taxonomy list) passes 1000 published visible documents, the static export drops the rest with no error and no failed build: posts vanish from المجلس and their pages 404 after the next deploy. Far off today; the failure is silent, which is what is worth fixing before it is forgotten.
findings.proposed_fix: Page the request (Range: 0-999, then the next page until the Content-Range total is reached), or fail the build when the returned row count equals the page size.

findings.title: Contact messages whose notice never reaches any staff mailbox are kept forever (no retention path)
findings.evidence: finance.contacts_purge selects only contacts with an outbox row `status = 'sent' ... and sent_at < now() - interval '90 days'`. A notice exhausted after 8 attempts, swept as RECIPIENT_INACTIVE (recipient demoted or revoked; 20261002120000_order_emails.sql:284-301) or marked suppressed because the staff address hard-bounced (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:646-659) is never sent, so its contact never qualifies, and RECIPIENT_INACTIVE rows cannot be replayed (outbox_replay refuses them), so nothing can ever make such a contact eligible.
findings.impact: The visitor's name, email and message stay in public.contacts indefinitely, against D36 (90 days) and docs/privacy-data-map.md:9, and the visitor is never answered. Precondition: a period in which the only owner/operations address was suppressed, the team had no active owner or operations member with an email, or the notices exhausted (a Resend outage spanning 8 attempts).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a second purge rule for the owner to approve: a contact whose every outbox row is exhausted, suppressed or RECIPIENT_INACTIVE for more than 90 days is deleted too, and surface such contacts on the owner home or البريد so the message is read before it goes.
findings.prior_overlap: D36 documents the 'stays until one does' rule; the never-delivered branch was not recorded

findings.title: Revoking a member bans and deactivates but does not end their sessions; the plan says it signs them out
findings.evidence: set_active false: `admin.from('staff').update({ active })` then `updateUserById(userId, { ban_duration: '876000h' })`; no `auth.admin.signOut(userId)` and no session delete. PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:99 says 'Removing a staff member sets active=false and signs out their sessions'.
findings.impact: Functionally safe: every policy and Edge Function re-reads staff.active, so the revoked member gets nothing on the next query, and the ban stops refresh and sign-in; the access token merely expires within jwt_expiry (3600 s). Only the plan sentence is inaccurate, and auth.sessions keeps the rows until privacy_erase_staff.
findings.proposed_fix: Either call `admin.auth.admin.signOut(userId, 'global')` after the ban (one line), or change the DATA-AND-SECURITY.md sentence to 'bans the Auth user and deactivates the row'.

findings.title: The last-owner guard's concurrency claim is proven by reasoning only; no test runs two demotions at once
findings.evidence: The comment states that two concurrent demotions of the last two owners cannot both pass (deferred constraint trigger + pg_advisory_xact_lock under READ COMMITTED). tests/integration/staff-admin.test.ts:106-127 demotes sequentially on one client; no integration test opens two connections. Reading the code the claim holds: the trigger function is VOLATILE, so its EXISTS query takes a fresh snapshot after the lock, which the first committer releases only at commit.
findings.impact: None found; recorded so the orchestrator can prove the non-negotiable invariant at runtime instead of trusting the comment.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one integration test: create owners A and B, open two pg connections, run `update public.staff set role = 'editor' where user_id = $A` and the same for B in two transactions committed concurrently; expect exactly one 23514.
findings.proof_recipe: Two psql sessions on the local stack: S1 `begin; update public.staff set active=false where user_id='<ownerA>';` S2 `begin; update public.staff set active=false where user_id='<ownerB>';` S1 `commit;` S2 `commit;`. Expected: one commit succeeds, the other fails with 'At least one active owner is required.' (23514). Wrong result: both commit and `select count(*) from public.staff where role='owner' and active` is 0.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 DB-media-3 noted the same sequential-only pattern for media_claim

findings.title: A 'suppressed' outbox row can never be replayed, even after the owner removes the suppression by hand
findings.evidence: outbox_replay: `if o.status not in ('exhausted', 'uncertain') then raise exception 'Only exhausted or uncertain messages can be replayed.'`; outbox_claim's due set is `status = 'pending' or (status = 'uncertain' ...)` (lines 319-322), so a row that outbox_claim set to 'suppressed' (lines 277-282) has no transition out. docs/operations.md:300-301 says re-allowing a recipient is 'a deliberate manual database action' and names only finance.email_suppressions; src/components/admin/EmailView.tsx:46-48 shows suppressed rows under «انتهت» with no replay button.
findings.impact: After a false hard bounce on the owner's own address (Resend reports the type as Permanent, or omits it) every contact notice and owner alert queued meanwhile becomes 'suppressed'; when the owner deletes the suppression row the mails still never go: البريد lists them as ended, and the only way out is a second hand-written UPDATE of finance.email_outbox that no runbook describes. The contact messages behind them then also fall under DB-CORE-08.
findings.proposed_fix: In outbox_replay accept `o.status = 'suppressed'` once the suppression check above it has passed (it already refuses a still-suppressed recipient), let EmailView offer the button for such rows, and add the step to the Suppression section of docs/operations.md.

findings.title: Edits to a media row's descriptive columns, including the rights text, leave no audit row
findings.evidence: `grant update (name, folder, alt_ar, caption, rights) on public.media to authenticated;` with media_staff_update (owner/editor) and only the media_touch trigger; media_rename_folder (line 164) is security invoker with no audit insert either. The only media audit rows are media.create (purpose, bytes) and media.delete (name).
findings.impact: An editor can rewrite the provenance text of any image (DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:95 makes rights a required record) and nobody can later see who changed it or what it said; media has no version history like content_versions. No money or access impact.
findings.proposed_fix: A small AFTER UPDATE trigger on public.media that inserts an audit_events row naming the changed columns (and from/to for rights), in the style of catalog_audit.

plan_gaps.title: Verify the hosted project's default privileges for service_role and the auto-expose toggle before launch
plan_gaps.why_needed: The migrations revoke anon/authenticated defaults only; what service_role holds on every table and function in public depends on the hosted project's creation date and the dashboard toggle (Supabase changelog 45329; local evidence in artifacts/acceptance/P03/commands.txt:45-46). The plan's grant statements (DATA-AND-SECURITY.md lines 10, 23, 49) are written as facts but only the local stack has been checked.
plan_gaps.touches: supabase/migrations (one forward migration revoking service_role defaults and keeping the grants staff-admin uses), PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md, PLANS/VERIFICATION.md (a hosted pg_default_acl check)

plan_gaps.title: Decide who may publish the policies collection and enforce it in SQL
plan_gaps.why_needed: DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:51 says the owner configures policies; src/admin/collections/policies.ts says editors draft and publish them; content_assert_publisher admits editors to every collection and publishing a policy resets the owner's approval and closes checkout (DB-CORE-01). The two documents cannot both be right and the DB enforces neither.

plan_gaps.title: A retention rule for contact messages whose notice never reached anyone
plan_gaps.why_needed: D36 keeps a message until a notice reaches a staff mailbox; a notice exhausted, suppressed or swept as RECIPIENT_INACTIVE never does, so such messages are kept for ever with no screen that lists them (DB-CORE-08, DB-CORE-11). E08 (privacy text and retention) is the natural place.

doc_claims_checked.claim: Custom Access Token hook: authentication_method takes the values oauth, password, otp, totp, recovery, invite, sso/saml, magiclink, email/signup, email_change, token_refresh, oauth_provider/authorization_code, anonymous, and the hook runs before every token issuance including token_refresh

doc_claims_checked.claim: Supabase stops granting new public tables and sequences to anon, authenticated and service_role by default: new projects from 2026-05-30, existing projects on 2026-10-30; the toggle is `alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke select, insert, update, delete on tables ... revoke usage, select on sequences from anon, authenticated, service_role`; only the public schema is affected
